turns.en: Well, I want to separate out some of the pieces of it. So things like putting precise probabilities on very hard to quantify outcomes.
turns.zh: 嗯，我想把其中的一些部分拆开来看。比如给那些非常难以量化的结果标上精确的概率这类事。

turns.en: There's a culture of that.
turns.zh: 这方面是有一种文化的。

turns.en: That culture, I think, is actually a very tough one to operationalize, right? Because again, there definitely are people who like to do that, but I don't know that that actually leads to real action, right? It doesn't lead to like real conclusions. And I think that That part of how I view it is that I think that the underlying question, right, the underlying question of this technology, like, what does it mean to build it right? Like, why are we building in the first place? Why are we all here? Why did we start OpenAI? Like, all of that, I think that that underlying question of this kind of risk and mitigating it and leaning into it and not shying away from the uncomfortable questions, that culture, absolutely prevalent. And so to me that a lot of how we've thought about open AI and other labs may be different. I can't comment on them, but I can just say at open AI is that we've really tried to think about we are here because we think that this technology, it's going to be the most transformative technology ever. That we think that it does have risks that we need to, as leaders, really lean into and mitigate. And that that is core. And that I think that we believe that, again, we have a lot of optimism that we can navigate. But again, it comes to this leadership this soberness, this taking the mission seriously. And at the end of the day, like we think that we will, like the reason we do it is for the benefits, for the fact that it can lift everyone up. But you only get there by really engaging in all these hard questions.
turns.zh: 那种文化，我觉得其实非常难以落地，对吧？因为再说一次，确实有人喜欢那样做，但我不知道那是否真能带来实际的行动，对吧？它带不来真正的结论。而我认为，我看这件事的方式是：那个根本问题，对吧，这项技术的根本问题——构建它意味着什么？我们当初为什么要构建它？我们为什么都在这里？我们为什么要创立 OpenAI？所有这些——我认为，那种围绕这类风险、去缓释它、去正视它、并且不回避那些令人不适的问题的根本追问，那种文化，是绝对普遍的。所以对我来说，我们思考 OpenAI 的很多方式，可能跟其他实验室不一样。我不能替它们评论，但我可以就 OpenAI 来说：我们真的努力去这样想——我们之所以在这里，是因为我们相信这项技术将会是有史以来最具变革性的技术；我们相信它确实有风险，而我们作为领导者，需要真正去正视并缓释这些风险；而这一点是核心。我认为我们相信——同样，我们非常乐观，相信我们能渡过。但归根结底，这要靠这种领导力、这种清醒、这种对使命的认真对待。而说到底，我们认为我们会成功——我们做这件事的原因是为了那些好处，为了它能托举每一个人这个事实。但你只有真正投入到所有这些难题里，才能走到那一步。

turns.en: And the thing I keep thinking is when it comes to AI development and safety, you're in addition to competing with other labs, you're competing in some respects against the models themselves, which are becoming smarter and smarter and more self-recursive in terms of their development. And those models, as the Hugging Face incident showed, seem to be very good at coordinating in an extremely rational, often literal way.
turns.zh: 而我一直想的是，在 AI 开发和安全这件事上，你除了要与其他实验室竞争，在某些方面你还在与模型本身竞争——它们正变得越来越聪明，而且在自身开发上越来越具有自我递归性（self-recursive）。而这些模型，正如 Hugging Face 事件所展示的，似乎非常擅长以一种极其理性、往往还很字面化的方式进行协调。

turns.en: Oh, shoot. So if you go to ChatGPT right now and you ask it for some script to hack into... you know, maybe you want to hack into my website or something like that. It's just not going to- No, I really don't. Yeah, I know.
turns.zh: 哦，糟了。我忘了问 Greg，他认不认同 Dwarkesh 用来形容那些模型的那个所谓的'三个文明'（three civilizations）框架，因为那会牵扯出一整套别的东西。你知道，还有一点是：似乎存在某种版本的安全，本质上就是把护栏（guardrails）立着，对吧？所以如果你现在去 ChatGPT，问它要一段能黑进……你知道，也许你想黑进我的网站之类的脚本，它就是不会给——不，我真的不想。是啊，我知道。

turns.en: There's nothing in there.
turns.zh: 那里面什么都没有。

turns.en: It's just not going to, it would be capable of producing the tech, but it won't. But that's just because there's a classifier model on there. And so, okay, part of the hugging face incident and maybe what's going to change is that some of these cybersecurity classifiers, these like very like kind of crude technology that just gates type of certain types of talk like it won't be allowed. That may be very helpful. That still doesn't strike me as alignment per se, because in the ideal world, You would just have models that have internalized what most of us know that you shouldn't hack.
turns.zh: 它就是不会给。它其实有能力生成那种技术，但它不会。但那只是因为它上面挂了一个分类器模型（classifier model）。所以，好吧，Hugging Face 事件的一部分、以及也许会改变的一点是：其中一些网络安全分类器——这些还挺粗糙的技术，只是把某些类型的谈话直接挡掉、不允许——那可能会非常有帮助。但这在我看来仍然不算是对齐本身（alignment per se），因为在理想世界里，你应该拥有的，是那些已经把'我们大多数人都知道的道理'——也就是'你不该去黑客攻击'——内化了的模型。
